review.assessment: The change replaces UTF-8 byte counting with ASCII-only character counting by silently dropping all non-ASCII characters via `encode("ascii", "ignore")`. This successfully prevents multi-byte padding attacks but fundamentally shifts the length metric from codepoints/bytes to a strict subset count. Consequently, any password composed entirely of non-ASCII characters will be reduced to an empty string and fail validation regardless of its actual visual length.

findings.actual: False (all non-ASCII characters are stripped, yielding b'' with len 0)
findings.defect: Over-rejection of valid Unicode passwords due to silent character stripping. The original rule counted UTF-8 bytes, allowing any codepoint contribution to length. The new implementation discards all non-ASCII characters entirely, meaning passwords that meet the minimum threshold by grapheme or codepoint count will now fail validation.
findings.expected: True (passes the minimum length threshold by Unicode character count)
